summary: Iter65 overclaim-sweep verification: RENDERED DOM is 100% clean (all 8 user-facing overclaims fixed), but the SERVED HTML SHELL (/app/frontend/public/index.html route meta-map) still contains 8 banned 100%-claim strings + a 'Buy <slug>' fallback description. These leak on every public route to non-JS crawlers / Googlebot initial fetch. 14/18 pytest + 18/18 rendered-DOM Playwright assertions pass.

integration_issues.issue: /app/frontend/public/index.html still contains 8 banned 100%-claim strings that are served in <title>/<meta description>/<h1> for specific routes. Items: line 235 '100% Guaranteed' (/buyer-protection), line 239 '100% safe!' (/refund-policy), line 240 '100% protected by Buyer protection' + '100% Ticket Guarantee' (/fan-protect), line 270 '100% safe checkout with Buyer protection' (/payment-info), line 288 '100% Buyer protection' (/belgian-grand-prix-tickets), line 293 '100% Guaranteed' + 'From €129 – 100% Guaranteed' (/f1-spa-tickets), line 314 '100% buyer protection guaranteed' (/buy-f1-tickets-online). Also line 419 fallback builder `d='Buy '+sn+' tickets... 100% Buyer protection.'` still uses banned 'Buy' prefix + '100% Buyer protection'. overclaim_sweep.py missed these shell-level entries.

action_items: Run overclaim_sweep.py (or manual edit) ON /app/frontend/public/index.html to rewrite the 8 flagged tuples: replace '100% Guaranteed' -> 'Refund policy', '100% safe' -> 'Secure checkout', '100% Buyer protection' -> 'Buyer protection', '100% protected by Buyer protection' -> 'protected by Buyer protection', '100% Ticket Guarantee' -> 'Ticket Guarantee', '100% safe checkout with Buyer protection' -> 'Secure checkout with Buyer protection', '100% buyer protection guaranteed' -> 'Buyer protection included'.

Verified sellers, QR ticket delivery, 100% Buyer protection.'` to `d='View '+sn+' tickets at Europe\'s verified listings. After edit: `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend` (webpack-dev-server caches public/index.html in memory) and re-run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_honesty_iter65_overclaim_sweep.py -v` — all 18 assertions should pass.
critical_code_review_comments: Shell meta-map and shell JS fallback description builder were NOT covered by overclaim_sweep.py even though iter64 main agent already knew the shell is a separate code path (see iter64 fix: index_html_honesty.py). Recommend consolidating shell sweeps in one script that always runs for ALL banned terms, not just the ones in iter64.

Fallback description builder at lines 419 + 430 reconstructs copy from slug when no meta tuple exists. Once the 8 tuples are cleaned, any new route will still inherit the softened copy automatically — good. Keep the fallback as the single source of truth for new pages.

Hub pages (Real Madrid, Liverpool) correctly set `<meta robots>` to 'index, follow' when real inventory exists (10 listings at €79 for Liverpool) and 'noindex, nofollow' when inventory is absent (Barcelona). EditorialByline E-E-A-T block renders correctly with office/support/last-reviewed-date. No action needed.

Rendered homepage fully compliant: hero = 'FIFA WORLD CUP 2026 TICKETS' + 'Secure checkout with QR ticket delivery', price card = 'FROM €150 / based on current listings', CTA labels = 'VIEW WORLD CUP TICKETS' + 'EXPLORE EVENTS', 5-badge trust strip only (no duplicate ticker), footer shows 'Refund available according to our refund policy', ReviewsSummary shows neutral line.

rca of the issue: RCA: overclaim_sweep.py targeted src/*.jsx components successfully (52 files, rendered DOM clean) but did NOT extend to public/index.html route meta-map tuples or the dynamic description builder at lines 419+430. Reproduction: `curl -sL https://euro-indexing.preview.emergentagent.com/ -A 'Mozilla/5.0' | grep -oE '100%[^"<>]{0,40}' | sort -u` returns 8 banned occurrences. Mitigation: patch /app/frontend/public/index.html directly at the 8 listed lines, restart frontend, re-run pytest. Impact: Googlebot that fetches raw HTML (initial crawl, before JS executes) sees the banned claims as the meta description / title — honesty-layer leak for SEO. Users (rendered DOM) are unaffected.
